title: Sequence shape scheduling & kernel strategy - working notes
content:
Purpose

This is a working note capturing design options and rough experiments for handling dynamic sequence shapes across: padding policies, bucketing heuristics, kernel selection, and interaction with the KV cache. Goal: reduce wasted compute from padding while preserving latency SLOs and predictable throughput for multi-tenant workloads.

Background / problem statement

- Our current default is simple per-batch max-length padding. That is easy but wastes tokens for long-tail sequences (common in chat + retrieval pipelines).
- We observe 3x token inflation on some workloads and tail latency regression when guests with long sequences monopolize GPU cycles.
- Kernel performance is non-linear in sequence length: some kernels favor short sequences more (lower overhead amortization), others scale better for long sequences.
- KV-cache state complicates batching: cached prefixes mean effective dynamic length varies by request and by model variant.

Design constraints / non-goals

- Must not violate customer-configured latency SLOs (p99 targets).
- Should be incremental: start with scheduler-level heuristics before heavy runtime fusing changes.
- Non-goal: full compiler rewrite. Focus on routing/scheduling + small kernel-selection rules.

Proposed building blocks (summary)

1) Fast lightweight length estimation at ingress
   - Tokenize and compute source_len and expected_generated_len estimate (from prior stats or query param). Add a small shape-hash to request metadata.

2) Adaptive bucketing layer in the scheduler
   - Hybrid buckets: high-resolution for short seqs (1..128: bins 8,16,32,48,64,96,128), coarser for long tails (256,512,1024+).
   - Time-windowed bucket resizing: buckets split/merge based on observed distribution over 10s windows to avoid fragmentation.

3) Padding policies (pluggable)
   - conservative-pad: pad to bucket representative (minimal waste, more buckets).
   - latency-pad: pad up to X percentile (default p90) of the bucket to meet latency SLO. Good for p99-sensitive customers.
   - kv-aware-pad: if request has hot KV presence (large cached prefix), pad against uncached suffix only.

4) Kernel selection rules (coordinator-driven)
   - Tag kernels by length-optimized ranges (short-kernel <=128, mid-kernel 129..512, long-kernel >512). Coordinator picks kernel based on bucket representative.
   - Secondary metric: batch size. If batch_size small and length short, prefer 'low-latency' kernel variant (fused attention tiling). If batch_size large, prefer throughput-optimized kernel.

5) KV-cache interaction patterns
   - Cache-warmup hint: warm requests (cache hit on prefix) can be batched separately since attention compute is only on suffix. Maintain separate cached-buckets.
   - Cache eviction awareness: when a request's cache miss rate is high, tag as 'cold' and avoid mixing with warm batches to reduce uneven compute.

Scheduling algorithm (sketch)

- Ingress: estimate effective_length = max(source_len, estimated_gen_len) - cached_prefix_len_hint
- Assign to bucket B based on effective_length and tenant affinity tags (SLA, priority)
- For each bucket, maintain two FIFO queues: warm-cache and cold-cache. Try to form batches within a latency window W (e.g., 20ms).
- If a high-priority request approaches deadline, use deadline-driven fast-path (pad to nearest bucket rep and dispatch immediately to low-latency kernel).

Micro-config examples (pseudo YAML for console)

- bucket_policy: hybrid
  - short_bins: [8,16,32,48,64,96,128]
  - long_bins: [256,512,1024]
  - adapt_window_ms: 10000
- padding_policy: kv-aware-pad
- latency_percentile: 90
- deadline_fastpath_ms: 10

Kernel selection pseudo-rules (coordinator config string)

- if effective_len <= 128 and batch_size >= 8 -> kernel: short_throughput_fused
- if effective_len <= 128 and batch_size < 8 -> kernel: short_lowlatency
- if 129 <= effective_len <= 512 -> kernel: mid_throughput
- if effective_len > 512 -> kernel: long_sparse_optimized

Performance expectations (rough)

- For mixed webchat workload (median 32, tail 800): expect 25-40% token cost reduction vs naive max-pad when using hybrid buckets + kv-aware-pad.
- P99 latency should hold or improve for latency-tuned tenants using deadline_fastpath. Tradeoff: more buckets -> higher scheduling overhead; mitigate by keeping adapt_window coarse when under 50% GPU utilization.

Risks and failure modes

- Bucket fragmentation: too many tiny buckets reduce batch formation and hurt throughput. Mitigation: TTL-based bucket merge and adaptive thresholds.
- Incorrect length estimates (e.g., user generates much more than estimate): can increase re-schedules or force kernel fallback mid-generation. Need fast fallback path: allow on-the-fly kernel switch for long-running generations.
- KV-cache tagging misses: inaccurate cached_prefix_len_hint leads to mis-bucketing. Mitigation: conservative default (assume uncached) and aggressive instrumentation.

Instrumentation & experiments to run

- Collect per-request: source_len, estimated_gen_len, cached_prefix_len_hint, bucket_assigned, kernel_used, batch_size, latency, token_cost
- A/B test: baseline vs hybrid-buckets+kv-aware-pad on a controlled tenant set for 2 weeks. Track p50/p95/p99 latency, cost/token, percent of wasted padding tokens.
- Microbench kernels: run synthetic sweep to measure kernel throughput curves vs seq length and batch_size; store in small lookup table used by coordinator.

Open questions / TODOs

- Fast on-the-fly kernel swap: can we pre-allocate kernel-compatible buffers so a request can migrate when length jumps? (Action: spike with PR #1789).
- How to prioritize cross-tenant fairness when short-seq spike floods the fleet? Consider 'shape-aware backpressure' on ingress load balancing.
- Integration with model-quantization profiles: certain quantized kernels behave worse on short sequences. Need joint kernel selection matrix.

Immediate next steps

- Evan: run kernel microbench and produce throughput curves (JIRA-INF-4823)
- Priya: implement bucket assignment + padding policy prototype in scheduler branch (link PR when ready)
- Liu: add telemetry schema and dashboards for pad-waste, bucket-utilization
- Asha: coordinate small internal A/B and write up a short runbook for ops to enable/disable per-tenant.

Notes / chatter

- See slack thread: #serving-runtime-shapes for recent field reports (esp. 2025-09-12 onward).
- Related work: prior dynamic-shape-padding-bucketing-spec.json (legacy) - this doc intentionally explores KV-aware padding and deadline fast-paths.

End of notes
